s01.text: Every Windows user has stared into the Blue Screen of Death. The popular legend says Microsoft picked blue because psychologists found it calms panicked users.

s02.text: That story is completely false. The color was decided in 1991 by one engineer, solving an annoying personal problem.

s03.text: John Vert was writing the Windows NT crash handler. When the kernel panics, display drivers are dead, leaving only raw 16-color VGA text mode.

s04.text: Vert's development machine was a MIPS RISC workstation. Its hardware firmware booted into bright white text on a deep blue screen.

s05.text: His favorite text editor, SlickEdit, also defaulted to white on blue. Vert spent his entire workday staring at blue terminals.

s06.text: So when Vert coded the crash screen, he picked the exact same blue. That way, he could boot, write code, and crash his machine without the monitor ever flashing.

s07.text: Thirty years later, over a billion PCs crash in that exact shade — not for psychology, but because one developer hated screen flicker.
